newsitem.title: USA: Senate Banking counsel optimistic on bank reform.
newsitem.headline: Senate Banking counsel optimistic on bank reform.

text.p: A Senate Banking Committee official said Thursday he was optimistic the next Congress will be the one to pass legislation repealing a Depression-era law separating commercial and investment banking.
"I think the stars finally are aligned properly to get Glass-Steagall reform in this Congress," Robert Giuffra, chief counsel at the Senate Banking Committee, said.

The Senate will also be more active initially in the session on banking issues, he told Reuters after a panel discussion sponsored by The Federalist Society. In the past Congress the Senate had waited to see House action first.
The banking bill that Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, R-NY, initially introduces could be even broader than the one he introduced in the last Congress, Giuffra said.
D'Amato had proposed allowing banks, insurance firms, securities companies and commercial firms to own one another.
"All options are open," Giuffra said. The Senate banking bill "will be something similar to the old bill, but perhaps broader even than that bill," he said.
